descriptionChirho: The Greek noun ὑπόδημα referring to a sandal or piece of footwear, the standard foot covering in the ancient Near East. All 10 NT occurrences carry the same referential meaning—a leather sole bound to the foot with straps. The two clusters differ only in grammatical number: S78177 (7x, accusative/genitive neuter plural 'sandals') and S78178 (3x, accusative/genitive neuter singular 'sandal'). Multilingual translations confirm a single sense: Spanish 'sandalias/sandalia,' Arabic 'حذاء/نعل,' Hindi 'जूते/जूती,' Korean '신발/신,' Swahili 'viatu/kiatu.' The singular-plural distinction is purely inflectional and does not warrant separate lexicographic senses.
